title: Empty groups, empty columns and no-results pages look as designed
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View, Work orders > Create & Edit and See financial data, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is 1440 px wide, with the browser zoom at 100%.
  • The design pictures DC-18-tech-technician-chosen-light-1440.png and DC-13-tech-search-empty-light-1440.png are open beside the app at 100% zoom (actual size); they are attached to this case.
  • The first picture shows an empty group at its bottom (Cameron Williamson, 0); the second shows the search-only empty page. The design's words differ from the PRD's ("No work orders assigned", "No results for …"); the case follows the PRD's words, so compare the look and the place only.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST DC13 Sam Idle) is an active technician at {Location-A} who leads no work orders and is used by this case only.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is chosen in any filter, Assigned to me is off, Search is empty and density is Regular (the default).
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Tech View in the display switcher.
  2. Look at {Technician-A}'s group.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  4. Look at {Technician-A}'s column.
  5. Click the Status filter and tick Paid.
  6. Type zzzz in Search.
  7. Look at the page.
  8. Click List in the display switcher and look at the page.
  9. Click Tech View in the display switcher and look at the page.
  10. Click Clear all filters.
  11. Type zzzz in Search.
  12. Look at the page.
  13. Click List in the display switcher and look at the page.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: under {Technician-A}'s header the group shows the words "No work orders" in grey, centred, with the clipboard outline icon before them, and no rows, as in the empty group at the bottom of the first design picture.
  • Step 4: the empty column shows a dashed rounded box holding a small light-grey circle with the clipboard outline icon and the text "Drag a work order here to assign it".
  • Step 7: the board is replaced by an empty state centred on the page: a round grey icon, the title "No work orders match these filters", the hint "Try removing a filter to widen your results." and a Clear all filters button.
  • Step 8: List shows the same empty state, with the same icon, words and button.
  • Step 9: Tech View shows the same empty state as List.
  • Step 12: Tech View shows "No work orders match the search "zzzz"." with no button, centred like the search-only design picture.
  • Step 13: List shows the same message as Tech View at step 12.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View), SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View), SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 52 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S2-R15, S3-R20, S1-R9a, S1-N1, S1-N1a and S1-N1b, read 14 Oct 2026; Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html", states states__work-orders__tech-technician-chosen__light__1440 (empty group) and states__work-orders__tech-search-empty__light__1440, and the empty-column block of Work Orders.dc.html (design pictures DC-18-tech-technician-chosen-light-1440.png, DC-13-tech-search-empty-light-1440.png, rendered from that export at the width in the name), read 14 Oct 2026. Covers the design defects SV-11319 (reported 14 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward). Where the PRD says nothing about the look, the design is the source. Source-verified 14 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build.

The design's empty texts read "No work orders assigned" and "No results for …"; this case follows the PRD's words (question W-13 to the product owner, not yet answered). The design's no-results page uses List's magnifier icon while S1-R9a gives empty states the clipboard icon (question PQ-V06, not yet answered), so steps 7 to 13 compare with List and do not judge which icon.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R15: “A technician group with no work orders under the current filters, and an empty Unassigned group, show the text “No work orders”.”
  • S3-R20: “A technician column with no work orders under the current filters, and an empty Unassigned column, show “Drag a work order here to assign it” to a user who can reassign work orders (S4-N1), and “No work orders” to everyone else.”
  • S1-R9a: “The switcher uses the design’s icons at 20px: List is Lucide `list`, Tech View is `user-round`, Board View is `square-kanban`. In Tech View and Board View every other icon is the design’s Lucide icon too: density (`row-height` in Tech View, `card-height` in Board View), collapse chevron (`chevron-down`), pin and unpin (`pin` / `pin-off`), Invoiced or Paid lock (`lock`), Unassigned avatar (`user-round`) and empty states (`clipboard-list`). List’s icons are unchanged.”
  • S1-N1: “When the active filters or a search return no work orders, Tech View and Board View show the same empty state as the List, with the same messages and action.”
  • S1-N1a: “With filters active, with or without a search, the empty state reads “No work orders match these filters”, then “Try removing a filter to widen your results.”, with a Clear all filters button.”
  • S1-N1b: “With only a search active, the empty state reads “No work orders match the search "{search}".” and shows no button.”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Board View empty column: “border-radius: 8px; border: 1px dashed var(--sv-border-strong); background: var(--sv-surface);”
  • Design — Work Orders.dc.html, Board View empty column: “font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--sv-text-secondary);">Drag a work order here to assign it”
  • Design — SKILL.md (design library), empty states: “Empty-state illustrations are a deliberate omission — Shopview empty states are text only.”
